(added) ∙3 days ago (added) Clear excess inventory with Big Spring Sale 2026 (added) (added) Big Spring Sale is back March 25-31, with seven days of deals across more than 35 categories. As our largest overstock deal event, you can use this opportunity to improve your inventory health by submitting Outlet deals. (added) (added) Creating Outlet deals for your products can increase sell-through, improve cash flow, optimize capacity levels, and reduce total storage fees. Plus, Outlet deals will have additional promotional visibility during this sales event. (added) (added) To create an Outlet deal, follow these steps: (added) (added) 1. From the Seller Central main menu, hover over Inventory , and click FBA Inventory . (added) 2. To filter for eligible inventory, click Create Outlet deal in the Recommendation filter. (added) 3. From the drop-down menu in the Action column to the right of the eligible item, select Create Outlet deal . (added) 4. In the pop-up window, enter your price in the Outlet deal price box . Your price must be less than or equal to the maximum price. (added) 5. Review the start and end dates for your Outlet deal, then click Submit . (added) (added) You can submit your Outlet deals until March 20 to run your deal during Big Spring Sale. To learn more about Outlet deal eligibility, visit Amazon Outlet. (added) (added) For more details on this event, go to Everything you need to know about Amazon’s Big Spring Sale 2026. (into) (into) This change applies to the following users: (into) (into) * Sellers who are subject to delivery-date based reserve policies and can view deferred transactions on the Payments dashboard (into) * Developers who access transaction reports through the reports API (into) (into) The updated reports will provide a clearer view of accrued earnings for month-end reconciliation and financial reporting. (into) (into) By April 30, when you request a Transaction or Summary report for a period beginning January 1, 2025, you’ll notice three key improvements: (into) (into) * All posted transactions are in one place . Your reports will include both transactions that have already been released to your balance, as well as transactions that are deferred under delivery-date based policies. You no longer must download separate deferred transaction reports to view deferred activity. (into) * Activity is indexed by posted date . The Date/Time column in Transaction reports will reflect the transaction posted date, rather than the release date, or payout eligibility date. This posted date provides a more consistent view of activity during the period that you select. (into) * You have clear visibility into deferred versus released statuses in same report . There will be a new column in Transaction reports that shows whether a transaction is deferred or released. An additional column, Transaction Release Date, will indicate when the transaction was released. If a transaction remains deferred, the release date field will be blank. (into) (into) If you have existing integrations with third-party financial systems, we recommend that you update your mappings or scripts. Note that reports for periods before January 1, 2025, will continue to follow the prior format. We plan to roll out similar reporting updates for additional stores by June 30, 2026. (into) (into) For more information, go to Payment Date Range Transaction and Summary reports. (into) (into) To provide feedback on these updates, contact us at vosfx-spff@amazon.com.
